findings.reason: without a case for a run that does write a fragment, the node's gate passes with the duplication this plan exists to remove still in place.
findings.text: the deliverable clause "a landing no longer splices one into the plan's landed record" has no case that can fail: the only landed-record case is a promotion without a fragment leaving the record byte-identical, and a record with no fragment directory composes to its own bytes already, so that case passes on the unmodified code; the record is composed on read rather than at promotion (reckon/serve.py:2705) and the composer appends the body of every fragment under the plan's fragment directory while returning the record's own bytes byte-identical when that directory is absent (reckon/evidence.py:714-:759), so the case the change newly permits (a node writing the now-optional fragment) is the one case the done-when does not cover

findings.reason: §6's case can only pass if §3's permitted sources and cases are widened to include the fragment link, which is a §3 edit the plan does not currently specify.
findings.text: §6 requires "the closure overview of §3 links it from that node's row", but §3's deliverable at docs/plans/a-landing-is-recorded-once.html:44 fixes the overview's sources as a commit, a run id, a gate command with its exit status, a gate log path or a figure path, with no fragment path among them, and §3's done-when has no case for a fragment link; §3's "reads no fragment" is consistent with linking, but no node is asked to render the link, so a §3 node builds none and §6's case then fails on a dependency's omission

findings.reason: the plan must name the literal clauses to remove and require the search to find them at the base revision, or this half of the done-when proves nothing.
findings.text: "a search of the skill files for a required fragment and for the per-landing splice returns none" is not a measurable case: the requirement is a semantic property rather than a string, it is stated in five places across four files in four different wordings (skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md:337, skills/reckon-build/references/worker-protocol.md:215, skills/reckon-build/references/sprint-orchestration.md:420 and :510, skills/reckon-build/references/coordinator-reference.md:821), and the token also matches prose with nothing to do with it (skills/reckon-build/references/orchestrator-harness/claude-code.md:346-:360, and "do not fragment context" at coordinator-reference.md:694), so any pattern the implementer picks returns none even if the requirement survives in wording it did not search for; the case also carries no negative control

findings.reason: §1 is read as context by every node, and a coordinator reading the deferral will hold §6 out of the dispatch set the declaration map admits.
